Longer lags correlate with: higher Eddington ratios, redder colors, stronger optical FeII equivalent widths, higher iron ratios (UV FeII/MgII and optical FeII/Hβ), CIV broad absorption troughs, and lower CIV blueshift.
AI.conclusion: The persistent size discrepancy across luminosity ranges, combined with complex wavelength-dependent delay patterns, indicates that variable diffuse emission contamination is widespread in AGN continuum reverberation measurements, challenging standard disk interpretations and requiring more sophisticated models.

title: Binary disruption during the early phase of open clusters
comment: 19 pages, 15 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The binary fraction in young open clusters exceeds that of field stars, making the study of binary dynamical evolution in clusters essential for understanding the origins and evolution of field binaries. Using N-body simulations based on Gaia DR3 open cluster observations and assuming a 100\% primordial binary fraction, we investigated the early evolution of binary survival fractions in open clusters. We find that binary disruption has two stages, an initial rapid decline followed by a slower decrease, well described by two piecewise linear functions. The early disruption rate, $k_1$, follows a power-law relation with the cluster's initial density ($ ρ_\mathrm{0} $), with an index of approximately 0.56, driven by the disruption of wide binaries via close encounters. The transition time between the two phases, $t_\mathrm{b}$, also exhibits a power-law dependence on $ρ_\mathrm{0}$ with an index of about -0.46. The disruption rate also depends on binary parameters: high-$q$ and wide binaries are disrupted faster, while the dependence on eccentricity $e$ is less clear, likely due to its strong evolution. We developed and publicly released a Python tool to predict binary survival fraction evolution based on $ρ_0$, $P$ and $q$. Additionally, we also investigate how open cluster binaries contribute to the field population, and find that the escaped stars have a systematically lower binary fraction, likely due to mass segregation. Both populations show similar distributions of $ P $ and $e$, but lower-$q$ systems preferentially remain bound within clusters, the origin of which remains uncertain.

AI.tldr: Binary survival in open clusters follows two-phase disruption: rapid early decline then slower decrease, with rates dependent on cluster density and binary parameters (period, mass ratio).
AI.motivation: Young open clusters have higher binary fractions than field stars, so studying binary dynamical evolution in clusters is essential to understand the origins and evolution of field binaries.
AI.method: N-body simulations based on Gaia DR3 open cluster observations, assuming 100% primordial binary fraction, to investigate early evolution of binary survival fractions in open clusters.
AI.result: Binary disruption has two stages (rapid decline then slower decrease) described by piecewise linear functions. Early disruption rate follows power-law with cluster density (index ~0.56). Transition time also follows power-law with density (index ~-0.46). High-mass-ratio and wide binaries disrupt faster. Python tool released to predict binary survival fraction evolution.
AI.conclusion: Binary disruption in open clusters follows predictable patterns dependent on cluster density and binary parameters. Escaped stars have lower binary fractions due to mass segregation. Both populations show similar period/eccentricity distributions, but lower-mass-ratio systems preferentially remain bound in clusters.

title: Chemo-dynamical reconstruction of Milky Way globular cluster progenitors: age--metallicity relations and the universality of multiple stellar populations
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, submitted to A&A (abstract abridged; see journal version for full abstract)
summary:
Globular clusters encode the hierarchical assembly history of the Milky Way and the physics of multiple stellar populations. Using homogeneous stellar parameters for 69 Galactic globular clusters derived while modelling multiple populations, we reconstruct progenitor-specific age--metallicity relations (AMRs) and test whether helium-related multiple-population (MP) properties depend on progenitor origin once cluster mass and metallicity are controlled for.
  Ages, helium spreads ($δY$), mean helium abundances ($\bar{Y}$), and first-population fractions ($f_{\rm P1}$) are drawn from hierarchical Bayesian CMD modelling. Progenitor families are identified via chemo-dynamical clustering, AMRs reconstructed within a hierarchical Bayesian framework, and MP indicators tested for environmental dependence.
  Enrichment timescales are consistent with $τ\lesssim 2$\,Gyr, though individual progenitors prefer shorter values when fitted independently. The primary distinction is the extent of chemical evolution: most systems reach $Δ[\mathrm{Fe/H}] \sim 1.1$--$1.3$\,dex while Sagittarius achieves ${\sim}1.6$\,dex and higher terminal metallicities. Gaia--Sausage--Enceladus and low-energy/Kraken are the dominant accretion events. Neither $δY$ nor $\bar{Y}$ depends on progenitor origin; the mass--MP scaling is indistinguishable across in-situ and accreted systems. Sequoia clusters alone show higher $f_{\rm P1}$ at fixed mass and metallicity.
  AMRs carry fossil signatures of progenitor chemical evolution and mass hierarchy. Helium enrichment amplitude is regulated by cluster mass and blind to environment, pointing to universal cluster-scale formation physics, with the sole exception of a residual dependence in $f_{\rm P1}$, suggesting the enriched-star fraction retains a secondary environmental imprint.

AI.tldr: The study reconstructs progenitor-specific age-metallicity relations for Milky Way globular clusters and finds that helium-related multiple-population properties are primarily regulated by cluster mass, not progenitor origin, suggesting universal formation physics across different accretion events.
AI.motivation: To understand the hierarchical assembly history of the Milky Way through globular clusters and test whether multiple-population properties depend on progenitor origin once cluster mass and metallicity are controlled for.
AI.method: Used homogeneous stellar parameters for 69 Galactic globular clusters from hierarchical Bayesian CMD modeling, identified progenitor families via chemo-dynamical clustering, reconstructed AMRs within a hierarchical Bayesian framework, and tested MP indicators for environmental dependence.
AI.result: Enrichment timescales ≤2 Gyr; most systems reach Δ[Fe/H] ~1.1-1.3 dex while Sagittarius achieves ~1.6 dex; Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus and low-energy/Kraken are dominant accretion events; δY and Ȳ don't depend on progenitor origin; mass-MP scaling indistinguishable across in-situ and accreted systems; only Sequoia clusters show higher f_P1 at fixed mass and metallicity.
AI.conclusion: AMRs carry fossil signatures of progenitor chemical evolution and mass hierarchy. Helium enrichment amplitude is regulated by cluster mass and blind to environment, pointing to universal cluster-scale formation physics, with the sole exception of a residual dependence in f_P1 suggesting the enriched-star fraction retains a secondary environmental imprint.

title: Energy dependence of the X-ray power spectrum in NGC4051 and NGC4395
summary:
Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) exhibit strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum on a wide range of timescales, particularly in X-rays where fluctuations are both rapid and high amplitude. Power spectral density (PSD) analysis is commonly used to characterise this variability. Although AGN PSDs are typically well described by a bending power-law model, the dependence of the model parameters on photon energy has not been systematically investigated.
  We examine whether PSD parameters depend on energy using two highly variable, low-mass Seyfert galaxies, NGC4051 and NGC4395, as case studies. Using archival observations from XMM-Newton, Suzaku, and NuSTAR, we computed power spectra in six energy bands spanning 0.3-20 keV and fitted them with a bending power-law model to study the energy dependence of the PSD parameters.
  Power spectra derived from light curves obtained with different satellites and at different epochs are consistent within uncertainties, indicating that the X-ray variability process in both sources is stationary. For both AGNs we find that (i) the PSD bending frequency is consistent with being independent of energy, (ii) the high-frequency slope becomes flatter at higher energies, and (iii) the PSD amplitude decreases with increasing energy.
  These results place important constraints on models of AGN X-ray variability, such as the fluctuating accretion-rate model. Similar analyses of larger AGN samples are required to fully characterise the energy dependence of AGN power spectra.

AI.tldr: Analysis of X-ray variability in two Seyfert galaxies reveals energy-dependent PSD parameters: high-frequency slope flattens and amplitude decreases with increasing energy, while bending frequency remains energy-independent.
AI.motivation: AGN X-ray variability is characterized by power spectral density (PSD) analysis, but the energy dependence of PSD parameters (bending frequency, slope, amplitude) has not been systematically studied despite being crucial for constraining physical models.
AI.method: Used archival XMM-Newton, Suzaku, and NuSTAR observations of two low-mass Seyfert galaxies (NGC4051 and NGC4395). Computed power spectra in six energy bands (0.3-20 keV) and fitted them with bending power-law models to analyze energy dependence of PSD parameters.
AI.result: X-ray variability is stationary across different satellites and epochs. For both AGNs: (1) PSD bending frequency is energy-independent, (2) high-frequency slope flattens at higher energies, (3) PSD amplitude decreases with increasing energy.
AI.conclusion: These energy-dependent PSD patterns provide important constraints for AGN X-ray variability models (e.g., fluctuating accretion-rate model). Larger AGN samples are needed for comprehensive characterization of energy dependence in AGN power spectra.

title: \HI 21-cm Line Properties of the Nearby LIRG IRAS 04296+2923
comment: 22 pages, 19 figures, Accepted by A&A
summary: We present an analysis of archival Very Large Array (VLA) and Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) \HI\ 21 cm data, together with archival multi-band radio continuum observations, of the nearby luminous infrared galaxy IRAS~04296+2923. The system, located behind the Taurus dark cloud at a distance of $\sim$29 Mpc, forms a small galaxy group consisting of five members as revealed by the \HI\ imaging. IRAS~04296+2923 has a close companion, HI~0432+2926, with a projected separation of $\sim$40 kpc, a small line-of-sight velocity difference of $Δ$ v = 26 km s$^{-1}$, and comparable total \HI\ masses of order $10^{9}$~$M_{\odot}$. Both galaxies exhibit regular \HI\ velocity fields and characteristic double-horn profiles in the VLA and FAST data, accompanied by only subtle asymmetries and extended \HI\ structures, indicating rotation-dominated kinematics with early signs of weak tidal interaction. Radio continuum emission is detected only from IRAS~04296+2923 and is confined to its nuclear region, consistent with previous studies. Modeling of its multi-band radio spectrum reveals a significant contribution from free--free emission at high frequencies ($>$30 GHz) and a high FIR-to-radio flux ratio ($q_{8.4}\simeq3.2$), implying a young, dust-obscured nuclear starburst. Taken together, the regular \HI\ kinematics, the small velocity offset, and the group-scale environment favor an interpretation in which IRAS~04296+2923 and HI~0432+2926 form a gravitationally bound, orbiting galaxy pair embedded in a small group, rather than an advanced merger. In this context, the luminous infrared galaxy (LIRG) nature of IRAS~04296+2923 is more plausibly driven by internal processes, such as bar-induced gas inflow, possibly modulated by long-timescale, low-level tidal interactions with nearby group companions.

AI.tldr: Analysis of HI 21 cm and radio continuum data reveals IRAS 04296+2923 and its companion HI 0432+2926 form a gravitationally bound galaxy pair in a small group, with IRAS 04296+2923's LIRG nature likely driven by internal processes rather than advanced merging.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature and environment of the nearby luminous infrared galaxy IRAS 04296+2923 through analysis of its HI kinematics, radio continuum properties, and group membership, particularly to determine whether its LIRG status results from advanced merging or internal processes.
AI.method: Analysis of archival VLA and FAST HI 21 cm data, multi-band radio continuum observations, HI imaging to identify group members, velocity field analysis, spectral profile examination, and modeling of radio spectra including free-free emission contributions.
AI.result: The system forms a 5-member galaxy group; IRAS 04296+2923 has a close companion (HI 0432+2926) with 40 kpc separation and small velocity offset (26 km/s). Both show regular HI velocity fields with double-horn profiles, indicating rotation-dominated kinematics with weak tidal interactions. Radio continuum is confined to IRAS 04296+2923's nuclear region, with significant free-free emission at >30 GHz and high FIR-to-radio ratio (q8.4≈3.2), suggesting a young, dust-obscured nuclear starburst.
AI.conclusion: IRAS 04296+2923 and HI 0432+2926 form a gravitationally bound, orbiting galaxy pair in a small group rather than an advanced merger. The LIRG nature of IRAS 04296+2923 is more plausibly driven by internal processes (bar-induced gas inflow), possibly modulated by long-timescale, low-level tidal interactions with group companions.

title: Chemical radial gradients for the bulge-bar stellar populations from the APOGEE survey
comment: 26 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables; accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The Milky Way bulge-bar is composed of multiple populations. Using chemical and kinematical planes, we segregate six populations in a bulge-bar sample observed by the APOGEE survey: two with bar-driven orbits, two with eccentric orbits, and two with low-eccentricity orbits, each composed of low- and high-[Mg/Fe] stars. Our sample spans $-2.0\lesssim$[Fe/H]$\lesssim+0.5$ and Galactocentric distance $R_{Gal}$ $<6$ kpc. We use chemical abundances from APOGEE DR17 for the elements Mg, Si, Ca, Al, K, Mn, Co, Ni, and Fe, and from the BAWLAS catalog for Ce and Nd. We find that the low- and high-[Mg/Fe] stars with low-eccentricity orbits, which exhibit chemical and orbital characteristics similar to those of the low- and high-[$α$/Fe] disks, display slightly negative and positive metallicity gradients, respectively. This result for the low-[Mg/Fe] low-eccentricity stars indicates a break in the global thin disk metallicity gradient. The high eccentricity populations with both low- and high-[Mg/Fe] show approximately flat metallicity gradients. In general, the [X/H] gradients of all elements for all populations follow Fe, except for the neutron-capture elements Ce and Nd. For all elements, the high-[Mg/Fe] bar population shows a much steeper positive [X/H] gradient than the nearly flat gradient for the low-[Mg/Fe] bar stars. The positive [X/H] gradients observed among our high-[Mg/Fe] bar stars probably reflect an age variation along the peanut structure. This interpretation agrees with the N-body simulations. Such steep positive gradients have also been reported in some high-redshift (z$\sim$4--10) galaxies.

AI.tldr: The Milky Way bulge-bar contains six chemically and kinematically distinct populations with varying metallicity gradients, revealing complex formation history and age variations.
AI.motivation: To understand the complex structure and formation history of the Milky Way bulge-bar by identifying distinct stellar populations through chemical and kinematical analysis, and to investigate their metallicity gradients as clues to their formation processes.
AI.method: Used APOGEE DR17 chemical abundances (Mg, Si, Ca, Al, K, Mn, Co, Ni, Fe) and BAWLAS catalog data (Ce, Nd) to analyze a bulge-bar sample. Segregated six populations using chemical and kinematical planes: two bar-driven orbits, two eccentric orbits, and two low-eccentricity orbits, each with low- and high-[Mg/Fe] stars. Analyzed metallicity gradients across populations and compared with N-body simulations.
AI.result: Identified six distinct populations with different orbital characteristics and chemical compositions. Found varying metallicity gradients: low-[Mg/Fe] low-eccentricity stars show slightly negative gradients (indicating break in thin disk gradient), high-[Mg/Fe] low-eccentricity stars show positive gradients. High eccentricity populations show flat gradients. High-[Mg/Fe] bar stars show steep positive [X/H] gradients compared to nearly flat gradients for low-[Mg/Fe] bar stars. Ce and Nd gradients differ from other elements.
AI.conclusion: The steep positive [X/H] gradients in high-[Mg/Fe] bar stars likely reflect age variations along the peanut structure, consistent with N-body simulations. These gradients resemble those observed in high-redshift galaxies, suggesting similar formation processes. The distinct populations reveal the complex assembly history of the Milky Way bulge-bar.

title: The shocking features in the closest rich galaxy cluster Norma
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, published on ApJ, see https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/ae4226
summary: The merger shocks generated by the collision of galaxy clusters elevate the pressure within the intracluster medium, significantly influencing the evolution of embedded cluster galaxies. We detect a merger shock (Mach number $\sim 1.3$) on the northwest side of the closest rich galaxy cluster Norma (A3627), using XMM-Newton and Chandra data. The textbook ram pressure stripping (RPS) galaxy ESO 137-001 appears to be located in the post-shock region. The shock boosts RPS and may induce the formation of the brightest known X-ray tail behind a cluster late-type galaxy. Another prominent head-tail radio galaxy ESO 137-007, with one of the longest radio continuum tails ($> 500$ kpc), is also likely in the post-shock region. The shock may have reversed the upstream jet to a one-sided radio head-tail morphology. Moreover, the shock can strip and roll the jet cocoon into a vortex ring structure like a `smoke ring' behind the end of the jet as observed by the ASKAP data. Therefore, the cluster merger shock can remarkably change cluster galaxies. Furthermore, Norma is the second brightest non-cool-core cluster following the Coma cluster, with a cool core remnant on its southeast side. Its original cool core may be disrupted by cluster mergers and/or active galactic nuclei.

AI.tldr: A merger shock in the Norma galaxy cluster enhances ram pressure stripping of galaxies, creating extreme X-ray and radio tails, and may explain the cluster's disrupted cool core.
AI.motivation: To investigate how merger shocks in galaxy clusters affect embedded galaxies through enhanced ram pressure stripping and morphological transformations, using the Norma cluster as a case study.
AI.method: Analysis of XMM-Newton and Chandra X-ray data to detect and characterize a merger shock (Mach ~1.3) in the Norma cluster, combined with observations of galaxies ESO 137-001 and ESO 137-007 using X-ray and ASKAP radio data to study shock-induced effects.
AI.result: Detection of a merger shock on the northwest side of Norma cluster; shock enhances ram pressure stripping on ESO 137-001, creating the brightest known X-ray tail behind a late-type galaxy; shock likely reverses upstream jet of ESO 137-007 into one-sided head-tail morphology and rolls jet cocoon into vortex ring structure; Norma identified as second brightest non-cool-core cluster with disrupted cool core remnant.
AI.conclusion: Cluster merger shocks significantly alter galaxy evolution through enhanced ram pressure stripping, morphological transformations of radio galaxies, and disruption of cluster cool cores, demonstrating the profound impact of cluster-scale dynamics on member galaxies.

title: Comparison of Bar Formation Mechanisms. IIIA. The role of classical bulges in spontaneous bar formation
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures. will be submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome!
summary: We run a suite of $N$-body simulations to investigate how classical bulges affect bar formation and properties under the internal formation mechanism. We incorporate bulges of varying mass and compactness into disk galaxy models and evolve them in isolation to examine the resulting bar pattern speeds and growth timescales. A more massive/compact bulge increases the Toomre $Q$ stability parameter and the circular velocity in the central region, while decreasing the disk mass fraction. It therefore delays the onset of bar formation and increases the bar growth timescale; sufficiently strong bulges can suppress bar formation entirely. During the formation stage, bars exhibit higher initial pattern speeds and faster deceleration rates when the bulges become more massive or compact. This faster deceleration persists after the bar buckling phase, leading to slower-rotating bars in the secular growth stage. However, when the bulge's "diluting" effect on the measured bar strength is removed or reduced, all bars within the same disk share similar distributions in the pattern speed-bar strength ($Ω_p$-$A_2$) space during the secular growth stage. They also show comparable ratios of the co-rotation radius to the bar length ($\mathcal{R}=R_{\mathrm{CR}}/R_{\mathrm {bar}}$) in this stage. These results suggest that the bulge's influence on the pattern speed is more significant during the bar formation stage, while in the secular growth stage, the bulge's effect may be less important, and the disk component dominates the pattern speed evolution.

AI.tldr: Massive/compact bulges delay bar formation, increase growth timescales, and can suppress bars entirely. During formation, bulges cause higher initial pattern speeds and faster deceleration, leading to slower-rotating bars. In secular growth, bars show similar Ω_p-A_2 distributions and R_CR/R_bar ratios when accounting for bulge dilution effects.
AI.motivation: To investigate how classical bulges of varying mass and compactness affect bar formation, pattern speeds, and growth timescales in disk galaxies under internal formation mechanisms.
AI.method: N-body simulations of isolated disk galaxy models with bulges of varying mass and compactness, examining bar pattern speeds, growth timescales, and evolution through formation and secular growth stages.
AI.result: Massive/compact bulges increase Toomre Q and central circular velocity while decreasing disk mass fraction, delaying bar formation and increasing growth timescales. During formation, bulges cause higher initial pattern speeds and faster deceleration. In secular growth, bars show similar Ω_p-A_2 distributions and R_CR/R_bar ratios when accounting for bulge dilution.
AI.conclusion: Bulges significantly influence pattern speeds during bar formation stage, but in secular growth stage, bulge effects become less important and disk component dominates pattern speed evolution.

title: AstroSat-UVIT observations of a possibly interacting pair of galaxies in HCG 77
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables, published in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: We aim to study star-forming regions and the spectral energy distribution of two possibly interacting galaxies, PGC 56121 and PGC 56125, in the Hickson Compact Group 77. We utilized the far-ultraviolet (FUV) channel of the Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope (UVIT) on board AstroSat to observe and produce FUV images of the galaxies. Our FUV images are at a much higher resolution in comparison to those obtained from previous galaxy surveys by GALEX in the near-UV and those from PS-1, DSS. We have identified several star-forming regions in the two possibly interacting galaxies, PGC 56121 and PGC 56125. These two galaxies form a pair widely separated in redshift and are seen in projection. We also report the presence of a candidate tidal dwarf galaxy at the end of one of the tidal tails located to the east of the pair, and we identified three major star-forming regions in the tidal dwarf. The spectral energy distribution of three galaxies in the system is presented and analyzed to investigate the key physical properties, such as stellar mass, dust mass, total luminosity, and star formation history, of the three galaxies. Based on these observations and on a comparison with observations in radio, these three galaxies are probably part of a small group of interacting galaxies.

AI.tldr: FUV imaging of interacting galaxies PGC 56121 and PGC 56125 in Hickson Compact Group 77 reveals high-resolution star-forming regions, a candidate tidal dwarf galaxy, and spectral energy distribution analysis indicating interaction.
AI.motivation: To study star-forming regions and spectral energy distributions of possibly interacting galaxies PGC 56121 and PGC 56125 in Hickson Compact Group 77 using high-resolution FUV imaging from UVIT/AstroSat.
AI.method: Utilized far-ultraviolet (FUV) channel of Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope (UVIT) on AstroSat to obtain high-resolution FUV images; identified star-forming regions; analyzed spectral energy distributions to derive physical properties including stellar mass, dust mass, total luminosity, and star formation history; compared with radio observations.
AI.result: Identified multiple star-forming regions in both galaxies; discovered candidate tidal dwarf galaxy at end of eastern tidal tail with three major star-forming regions; spectral energy distribution analysis provided physical properties; comparison with radio observations suggests the three galaxies are part of an interacting group despite redshift separation indicating projection effect.
AI.conclusion: PGC 56121 and PGC 56125, though widely separated in redshift and seen in projection, are likely interacting galaxies within a small group, with evidence including star-forming regions, tidal features, and a candidate tidal dwarf galaxy revealed by high-resolution FUV imaging.

title: Comparing the $M_{gas}-N_{yso}$ Relation inside a Giant Molecular Cloud
comment: 12 pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: In this paper we present a simple analysis around scaling relations derived from the Schmidt conjecture for star-forming molecular clouds, at the intra-cloud scale. Using a hierarchical tree (dendrograms) above a constant threshold ($A_V$ = 7 mag), we separate individual gas structures in a column density map of the nearby Giant Molecular Cloud Orion A, constructed from Herschel far-infrared maps. These structures define regions of dense molecular gas that can actively form stars. We also estimate their current embedded population using a list of known young stars. From the combined analysis of the column density map and the young star catalog, we construct a series of plots that show the intra-cloud level behavior of three well-known scaling relations: $N_{yso}$ vs. $M_{gas}$, $Σ_{SFR}$ vs. $Σ_{gas}$ and $R_{eq}$ vs. $M_{gas}$. Our dataset, along with other sets from literature, show the validity of a linear relation for $N_{yso}$ vs. $M_{gas}$, from intra-cloud to inter-cloud scales, over three orders of magnitude. We also especulate on the possibility that the relation could be valid over an even larger scale range. Additionally, our data are consistent with the $R_{eq}$ vs. $M_{gas}$ discussed in previous studies. However, our data is not quite in agreement with previously proposed fits for the $Σ_{SFR}$ vs. $Σ_{gas}$ relation, and we discuss the implications of using the free-fall timescale as the main parameter defining the star-forming efficiency in dense gas regions.

AI.tldr: Analysis of intra-cloud scaling relations in Orion A molecular cloud shows linear N_yso vs M_gas relation across scales, supports R_eq vs M_gas relation, but disagrees with previous Σ_SFR vs Σ_gas fits, questioning free-fall timescale efficiency.
AI.motivation: To test scaling relations derived from the Schmidt conjecture at intra-cloud scales within star-forming molecular clouds, specifically examining how star formation properties relate to gas properties within individual cloud structures.
AI.method: Used hierarchical tree (dendrograms) above A_V = 7 mag threshold to separate individual gas structures in Herschel-derived column density map of Orion A. Combined analysis of column density map with young star catalog to construct scaling relation plots: N_yso vs M_gas, Σ_SFR vs Σ_gas, and R_eq vs M_gas.
AI.result: Found linear relation for N_yso vs M_gas valid from intra-cloud to inter-cloud scales over three orders of magnitude. Data consistent with R_eq vs M_gas relation from previous studies. Data disagrees with previously proposed fits for Σ_SFR vs Σ_gas relation, suggesting issues with using free-fall timescale as main parameter defining star-forming efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Linear N_yso vs M_gas relation appears robust across scales, while Σ_SFR vs Σ_gas relation requires re-evaluation of underlying assumptions, particularly regarding the role of free-fall timescale in determining star formation efficiency in dense gas regions.
